d.note: The original of the Rochester-area burger-and-hots chain, which still brews root beer in each store.
d.fn: Tom Wahl opened in Avon in March 1955 as a root beer stand in a trailer and kept adding on to the building (Tom Wahl's); now nine locations.

d.note: Monroe Avenue bagel shop in Brighton that NYSDOH lists as a bakery. Visit Rochester lists it.
Fairport Road hots shop whose take on the Rochester plate is called 'The Hot Plate'.
Henrietta hots shop named by Visit Rochester among local places to get a plate.
Ridge Road shop of the Schaller's burger-and-hots family, opened three years after the original drive-in.
d.fn: Schaller's says its Ridge Road shop opened in 1959.

d.note: Cantonese dim sum restaurant where diners order on iPads and baskets arrive on a two-level conveyor belt. The chef has more than 30 years of New York City dim sum experience.
d.fn: Its site says it opened in 2024. CITY (Nov 2025) calls it recently opened.

d.note: Family-run Rochester bagel shop with a long list of bagel and cream cheese flavors, plus breakfast sandwiches, soups and vegan options. NYSDOH lists it as a bakery.
Monroe Avenue hot dog shop offering 18 topping styles on Zweigle's franks in fresh French bread, plus meat and veggie plates.
Sea Breeze burger-and-hots stand between Irondequoit Bay and Lake Ontario, known for ground rounds and chocolate almond custard.
d.fn: Don Barbato leased a roadside stand at Sea Breeze in 1945 (as Don & Bob's) and later renamed his Sea Breeze location Don's Original; the listing says est. 1945. Not confirmed that the 1945 stand stood at 4900 Culver Rd.

d.note: Monroe Avenue hots counter that Visit Rochester lists among local spots for a Rochester plate; its version is the 'Sloppy Plate'.
Originator of the trademarked Garbage Plate: meats over home fries, macaroni salad, beans or fries, topped with mustard, onions and meat hot sauce.
d.fn: Founded 1918 by Alex Tahou as West Main Texas Hots and named for his son Nick (Wikipedia; the restaurant says 'since 1918'). In the mid-1950s the stand was in a smaller building just east of today's restaurant (the former Buffalo, Rochester & Pittsburgh Railway station), so 1918 is not the year at this building. 'Garbage Plate' trademark filed in 1991.

d.note: Lakeside drive-in that started the Schaller's burger-and-hots stands. Visit Rochester lists Schaller's among local spots for a plate.
d.fn: Schaller's says two brothers opened this original drive-in in 1956.

d.note: Lyell Avenue hots shop serving its "Famous Plates" with its own hot sauce, made with Zweigle's hots and white hots.
West Ridge Road hots shop. Visit Rochester names it (as Westridge Hots) among local places to get a plate.
